title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce automated tuning for batching and KV-prefix caching defaults, add model quantization profile support for runtime selection, and ship a first-pass unit-economics (UEcon) tooling integration that surfaces per-route cost recommendations and estimated savings. This PR includes: 1) controller logic to collect live latency/throughput samples and compute per-workload optimal batch size and cache defaults, 2) runtime changes to accept quantization profiles and fall back plans (int8/4-bit candidates with quality heuristics), 3) a UEcon CLI and API endpoint that aggregates token-level cost estimates and suggests config changes with expected savings, 4) dashboard hooks and telemetry for rollout monitoring, and 5) migration scripts and a non-disruptive rollout plan with canary + auto-rollback on quality regressions. Tests: unit tests for autotune heuristics, integration tests against the serving runtime simulator, and load benchmarks for representative workloads. Benchmarks show ~18-27% token-cost reduction for chat-heavy routes and 10-15% latency improvement under moderate concurrency in our internal canary region. Follow-ups: extend quant-profile scoring to include eval-driven quality deltas and add RBAC for UEcon actions (ENG-2039, ENG-2078).

release_notes: Adds autotune for batching and caching defaults to reduce per-token costs, introduces quantization profile support for runtime model selection, and ships a first-pass unit-economics tooling surface that recommends cost-saving config changes with estimated impact. Non-breaking: gated behind feature flag 'autotune_defaults_v1'.
